questions.text: What is the main purpose of a computer network?

options.B: To connect computers and allow them to share data and resources
options.C: To prevent viruses from entering the computer
options.D: To convert analogue signals to digital signals

questions.text: Which type of network connects computers within a single building or school campus?
What type of network is created when you connect a smartphone to a wireless speaker and a smartwatch using Bluetooth?
What technology does a Wireless LAN (WLAN) use to transmit data between devices?
Which network covers a large geographical area, such as connecting offices across different cities or countries?
What is the typical maximum communication range of Bluetooth?
Linking a smartphone to a laptop to share the mobile phone's internet connection is called:
What unique hardware identification number is permanently burned into a Network Interface Card (NIC)?
Why is a network Hub referred to as a "dumb" device?

options.A: It cannot be turned on or off
options.B: It broadcasts incoming messages to all connected computers
options.C: It requires an internet connection to function

questions.text: How does a Switch differ from a Hub?

options.A: It connects a LAN directly to a WAN
options.B: It reads the destination MAC address and sends data only to the intended recipient
options.C: It converts digital data to analogue signals
options.D: It only works using wireless signals

questions.text: Which network device is used to connect two separate segments of the same Local Area Network (LAN)?
What primary hardware device connects a local network to the Internet and directs traffic between different networks?
Which part of a data packet contains the sender and recipient IP addresses?
What is the main function of the Footer (Trailer) in a data packet?

options.A: To store the main message content
options.B: To provide error checking and indicate the end of the packet
options.C: To hold the MAC address of the router

questions.text: The process of breaking a file into small chunks, sending them across different network routes, and reassembling them at the destination is called:
What set of protocols governs the transmission of data across the Internet?
An Intranet is best described as:

options.A: A global public network accessible to everyone worldwide
options.B: A private network within an organization accessible only by its members
options.C: A temporary network created using Bluetooth
options.D: A public Wi-Fi hotspot in an airport

questions.text: What is an Extranet?

options.A: An internal network that has no security password
options.B: A network used exclusively for audio conferencing
options.C: An extension of an intranet that allows limited access to authorized external users
options.D: A satellite network used in deep ocean research

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of Cloud Storage for a business?

options.A: Files can be accessed from anywhere with an internet connection
options.B: It eliminates the need for an internet connection
options.C: Data is completely immune to cyberattacks
options.D: Users have 100% control over the physical server hardware

questions.text: A security device or software that inspects incoming/outgoing network traffic and blocks unauthorized access is a:
What type of encryption uses two different keys (a Public Key and a Private Key)?
In Asymmetric Encryption, which key is used to decrypt (unlock) the received message?
Which password follows the textbook criteria for a STRONG password?
Which of the following is a Biometric authentication method?
How does a computer Worm differ from a computer Virus?

options.B: A worm requires human action to spread
options.C: A worm is an independent program that spreads automatically across networks without human action
options.D: A worm only targets mobile phones

questions.text: What type of malware disguises itself as useful, legitimate software to trick users into installing it?
What is the primary function of Spyware?

options.B: To record keystrokes and secretly monitor user activities
options.D: To physically damage the hard drive

questions.text: Where does anti-malware software place suspicious, infected files so they cannot harm the rest of the system?
What equipment distinguishes Video-conferencing from standard Web-conferencing?

options.A: Web-conferencing uses large wall-mounted screens, room cameras, and dedicated private lines
options.B: Video-conferencing uses specialized high-quality room equipment and dedicated lines, whereas web-conferencing uses web browsers and laptops
options.C: Video-conferencing does not support video transmission

questions.text: A one-way, non-interactive video or audio transmission broadcast over the internet is called a:
The Internet is classified as a global Wide Area Network (WAN).
Bluetooth has a higher data transfer speed and longer range than Wi-Fi.
A MAC address changes every time a device connects to a new Wi-Fi network.
A Hub reduces unnecessary network traffic compared to a Switch.
Routers inspect IP addresses to forward data packets to the correct destination network.
In packet switching, all data packets belonging to the same message must travel along the exact same physical route.
Intranets can be accessed by any member of the general public without logging in.
Storing data on Cloud Storage removes the need for an active internet connection to access files.
A Firewall can be implemented as either software or a dedicated hardware device.
In Asymmetric Encryption, the Public Key is kept secret while the Private Key is shared openly with everyone.
Biometric security systems rely on something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.
Computer viruses need to attach themselves to another executable file or program to spread.
Adware is software designed to record user passwords by capturing keypresses.
Anti-malware software should be updated regularly so it can detect newly created threats.
A Webinar is an interactive online teaching session where participants can ask questions to the presenter.

sections.title: Section 3: Fill in the Blanks & Short Recall

questions.text: A network setup connecting personal mobile devices within a short distance of 1-10 meters is known as a PAN, which stands for ____________________.
MAC Address stands for ____________________.
The permanent, unique number burned into every Network Interface Card is called a ____________ address.
A device that links two separate segments of the same Local Area Network is called a ____________.
A data packet consists of three main parts: the Header, the ____________, and the Footer.
An IP address stands for ____________________.
The global, public system of interconnected computer networks is called the ____________.
A private network accessible only by internal employees or members of an organization is an ____________.
An intranet extended to grant controlled access to external partners (like suppliers or customers) is an ____________.
The process of scrambling data into an unreadable format using a key to keep it secure is called ____________.
Authentication using physical biological traits (such as fingerprint or iris scans) is known as ____________.
Malicious software specifically designed to secretively spy on user activities and log keypresses is called ____________.
Placing an infected or suspicious file into an isolated folder to prevent it from harming the system is called ____________.

Scenario: A teacher wants to send a printable document from her laptop to a network printer in the room next door without using a USB flash drive. Question: What network type connects these classroom devices together?

Scenario: Farhan is moving around the school library while working on his laptop without losing his internet connection. Question: What wireless network type enables Farhan to stay connected while moving?

Scenario: A small office has 8 computers plugged into a central box. Whenever Computer 1 sends a file to Computer 2, all other 6 computers slow down because they receive the same file data. Question: What "dumb" network device is currently installed in this office?

Scenario: The office in Q63 replaces the central box. Now, when Computer 1 sends a file to Computer 2, no extra traffic is sent to the other 6 computers. Question: What "smart" network device did they install?

Scenario: A company in Jakarta needs to connect its local office network to its branch office network in London. Question: What primary network hardware device is required at each location to direct traffic across the internet between these two networks?

Scenario: A hospital creates an internal portal where doctors can share patient medical records. Patients cannot log in to this portal from home. Question: What network environment is the hospital using? (Internet, Intranet, or Extranet?)

Scenario: The hospital updates its portal to allow patients to log in securely from their homes to book appointments with doctors. Question: What network environment is being used now? (Internet, Intranet, or Extranet?)

Scenario: A graphic design firm moves all its project files to Google Drive so designers can work from home. However, one day the local internet service goes down, and no one can work. Question: What major disadvantage of cloud storage does this situation highlight?
Scenario: An attacker intercepts data packets moving across a public Wi-Fi network without modifying any system settings or interrupting data flow. Question: What type of cyber attack is this called?

Scenario: An unauthorized user attempts to access a school's internal server from the internet. A security system inspects the incoming IP address, identifies it as untrusted, and blocks the connection. Question: What network defense mechanism performed this action?
Scenario: Alice wants to send a confidential document to Bob using Asymmetric Encryption. Question: Which of Bob's keys should Alice use to encrypt the document?
Scenario: Bob receives the encrypted document from Alice. Question: Which key must Bob use to decrypt and read the document?
Scenario: Student A creates the password "rover2015" (Rover is his dog's name). Question: Give two reasons why this password is considered weak according to textbook rules.
Scenario: A bank customer inserts a plastic card containing a microchip into an ATM and enters a 4-digit PIN. Question: What type of authentication card is this?

Scenario: A bank sends a 6-digit One-Time Password (OTP) to a customer's smartphone or key fob device to authorize an online transaction. Question: What type of authentication device is being used here?

Scenario: A user receives an email containing a link to download a free popular game. After running the installer, the user's files are suddenly deleted, even though no new windows appear. Question: What type of malware was disguised inside the game installer?

Scenario: A computer on a school network becomes infected. Within 10 minutes, 50 other computers on the same network become infected automatically without any student clicking on any links or opening files. Question: What type of self-replicating malware caused this infection?
Scenario: Every time a user opens a web browser, ten unwanted pop-up windows promoting shopping websites appear on the screen. Question: What type of malware is affecting the computer?

Scenario: A multinational bank holds an international board meeting between executives in Tokyo, London, and New York. They sit in dedicated rooms facing large TV displays with wall-mounted cameras and communicate over a private line. Question: Is this an example of Video-conferencing or Web-conferencing?

Scenario: A university lecturer hosts a live online teaching session over the internet where 100 students join using their web browsers on laptops, view the slides, and type questions in the chat box. Question: What specific type of web-conferencing session is this?
